verification_level: FAST plus the full library suite. One bounded mechanism change in cms_env.rs: key-unwrap output capacity is established before provider dispatch and the unwrapped content key has a single owner; both KEK and KTRI arms. No new hidden obligation, no ABI/layout/export change, no allocator-seam size/file/line change.
scope: src/cms/cms_env.rs, restricted to key unwrapping and content-key ownership: cms_RecipientInfo_kekri_decrypt, cms_RecipientInfo_ktri_decrypt, the staging/validation helpers, and the content-key owner. Not a whole-file conversion.

mechanism.trigger: CVE-2026-63072's write edge: EVP_DecryptUpdate is passed `in_len + block_size` as the provider's writable extent while CMS gives the unwrap output only `in_len - 8`; the produced length was checked only after the writes, and the reported length became ec->keylen (the extent a later OPENSSL_clear_free cleanses).
capacity_before_dispatch: KEK: declared_update_extent(wrapped_len, cipher block size) reproduces exactly the outsize EVP_DecryptUpdate passes (`in_len` for a one-byte block, `in_len + block_size` otherwise), checked with checked_add. A frame-private SecretScratch of exactly that extent is allocated before any provider call, so the provider is told the truth about the block it can fill.
KEK: content_key_extent(wrapped_len) = checked `in_len - 8`; the authority's content-key allocation stays at cms_env.c:995 with the same size/file/line.

KEK: the update's reported length is accepted only by reported_extent(report, stage.capacity()); it is then required to be <= the content-key extent before the final write pointer (stage + written) is constructed. The final report is validated against the remaining stage capacity and the total against the content-key extent. A larger report is refused, never used as an offset or as ec->keylen.

KTRI: the provider's own two-pass query is now performed in this function; the first EVP_PKEY_decrypt call establishes `capacity` before allocation or write, the block is allocated at exactly that extent (asymcipher.c:337 / :343 coordinates preserved), the second call is given `capacity` as its declared output extent, and `produced <= capacity` is required before adoption.

owner_design.kekri: SecretScratch (Rust Vec, zero-initialised, try_reserve_exact, cleansed over its whole extent in Drop) owns the provider's staged plaintext. OwnedBuf at cms_env.c:995 owns the content key; it is transferred into ec.key exactly once with into_raw(), with ec.keylen set to the validated produced length. Every failure after the allocation drops the OwnedBuf (cleansing release, single release); failures before it leave the slot untouched.
owner_design.ktri: A single OwnedBuf::new_cleansed_released(capacity, asymcipher.c:337, release :343) is the only owner from the moment the provider's extent is known. Validation failure drops it at :343 over the allocation extent; success transfers it into ec.key exactly once. The authority's ec destructor later releases it at cms_asn1.c:88 over ec.keylen = produced.

eliminated: The post-write unwrap_length_fits check as the only defence against a provider over-report: it could not establish the safety of writes that had already happened.
Direct provider writes into the in_len-8 content-key allocation: the provider now writes only into a block of exactly the extent it was told it could fill.
Production use of evp_pkey_decrypt_alloc's trust that the second-call report is within the first-call extent.
relocated: Provider output writes are confined to unwrap_staged + SecretScratch, an auditable boundary whose # Safety contract fixes the ctx, stage extent, key extent and input readability.
The KTRI seam allocation moved inside cms_env.rs but keeps the authority's exact coordinates and size derivation (asymcipher.c:337 malloc, :343 cleansing free).
new_unsafe_operations: SecretScratch::drop's OPENSSL_cleanse over its own allocation (narrow, documented).
unwrap_staged's # Safety contract and its two provider calls (narrow, documented; callers establish the extent relations).
removed_from_production: adopt_decrypted_key is now #[cfg(test)]: it remains the release-model witness that an installed ec.key is cleansed/released at cms_asn1.c:88, but the production path no longer adopts a helper block.

preserved.owned_buf_patterns: OwnedBuf::new_cleansed_released at cms_env.c:995 unchanged in arguments; into_raw remains the single transfer edge.
preserved.modes_wrap_cleansing_limits: src/modes/wrap.rs untouched; the CVE-2026-63072 cleanse-extent test still passes.
preserved.exported_symbols: none added, removed or re-signed; no #[no_mangle] diff.
preserved.allocator_seam: same sizes and coordinates: cms_env.c:995 (content key), asymcipher.c:337/343 (KTRI key). The added SecretScratch is a Rust allocation, not a CRYPTO_* event, so a caller-installed CRYPTO_set_mem_functions hook sees the same seam event stream.
preserved.error_reason_codes: CMS_R_INVALID_KEY_LENGTH, CMS_R_INVALID_ENCRYPTED_KEY_LENGTH, CMS_R_UNWRAP_ERROR and ASYMCIPHER_342 retained.

tests.filtered: cargo test --lib cms::cms_env -- --test-threads=4: 29 passed / 0 failed / 6 ignored (2171 filtered).
tests.negative_control: cms_env_negative_control_pre_fix_undersized_output_is_detected ... ok. It reconstructs the pre-fix pairing (declared extent in_len + block_size into a block of in_len - 8), asserts the pairing is exactly the defect (declared > key_capacity), and asserts the new detectors (reported_extent against the key extent; checked_add capacity arithmetic) fire on it. Test-only; no production path can reach it.

gates_observed.structural: git diff of src/cms/cms_env.rs contains no #[no_mangle], #[repr(C)] or exported-signature change; the only new extern "C" fns are test-local fake provider callbacks. No allocator-seam size/file/line change.
gates_observed.affected_probes: The four cms_env allocator probes run one per process under OPENSSL_RS_ADV_PROBE=1; all passed. Miri/ASan/Loom/const-time were not run (no aliasing, concurrency or secret-dependent-control mechanism changed).

historical_cve_replay.why: The candidate path is now drivable end-to-end and is exercised by the new unit tests, including the padded-wrap OID and a provider that over-reports. The historical replay's positive control, however, is an 8-byte heap OOB write in the vulnerable authority; making that observable requires a guard-page or ASan allocator in the replay venue, which courts/phase25/cve_replay_probe.c does not install for the historical authority (the probe still emits `unsupported` for this case). A replay with an unfired control is recorded UNKNOWN, never as a pass, so the record was deliberately not promoted.

residuals: The staging buffer doubles the transient plaintext footprint (content-key extent plus declared update extent). It is a Rust allocation, so it does not alter the CRYPTO_* seam event stream, and it is cleansed on drop.

A provider that lies about its produced length after writing can still write within the declared extent (now a real allocation); the report is detected and refused before it becomes an offset or ec.keylen, but a write beyond the declared extent cannot be detected without a sanitizer/guard-page instrument. This is a detection boundary, not a trust boundary.

The KTRI inline duplicates the two-pass shape of evp_pkey_decrypt_alloc because that helper does not expose the first-pass capacity. The helper itself is unchanged for its other caller; its own second-pass report is not hardened here (out of this target's scope).
Miri/ASan/Loom and a differential allocator transcript against the authority were not run at this level (BATCH evidence only for the focused probes).
non_claims: This does not discharge the whole src/cms unsafe surface or any consumer family's dependency closure.
The provider boundary is now sound against a conforming provider and detects over-reports; it is not a claim that a hostile in-process provider cannot corrupt memory through unrelated callbacks.
The CVE replay remains UNKNOWN; a unit-level exercise is not a historical replay.
